<div class="note-box">

**Where this sits.** Round 6 built the analytic MELD-λ0 target and showed on
synthetic 50/50 EUR/AFR that R\* beats every single-population panel by
0.11–0.25 r² on M2. Round 7 moves from synthetic to real sumstats
(Yengo-2022 all-ancestry height) and asks whether the composition effect
survives at 1KG panel scale on a realistic ~78 % EUR meta. Section 1 fixes
the pre-existing quickprs AF-difference LRT filter that Round 5
identified as a variant-count confounder, and adds a variant-intersection
helper that Section 4 will use. Section 2 runs M2 on the real sumstats and
validates the AF-projection composition estimator against the
paper-reported per-population sample sizes.

</div>

# Section 1 — code fixes

## S1.1 — quickprs.R AF filter option

Added `--skip_lrt_af_filter` boolean CLI option to
`Scripts/pgs_methods/quickprs.R`. Default `FALSE` preserves the existing
LRT filter (`P < 1e-6`) exactly. When `TRUE`, the LRT filter is skipped and
the upstream `sumstat_cleaner.R --maf_diff` (default 0.2) is the only AF
check.

Threaded through the pipeline:

- `pipeline/config.yaml` — new `quickprs_skip_lrt_af_filter: F` (default
  preserves behaviour)
- `pipeline/rules/pgs_methods.smk` — `prep_pgs_quickprs_i` params + shell
  command pass the flag through

Smoke-tested by direct invocation on chr22 with the Round-5 MELD refdir /
quickprs LD panel and the Round-5 cleaned sumstats:

- With `--skip_lrt_af_filter TRUE`: log records
  `Skipping LRT AF filter (--skip_lrt_af_filter TRUE); MAF-diff in sumstat_cleaner already handles this.`
- Without the flag: log records
  `Removed 8872 variants due to significant difference in allele frequency to reference (P < 1e-6).`
  — exact prior behaviour.

Backward compatibility confirmed. **Why this matters:** the LRT filter's
statistical power scales with the reference sample size $n_0$. On a
MELD-composed panel (1154 samples) the filter is far more aggressive than
on a single-population panel (665–737 samples). Round 5 saw
mismatched-cell removals of 390 k–500 k variants under single-pop LD but
611 k under MELD LD — the variant-count confounder is real, and any Round
5 method-comparison that varied $n_0$ between cells was reading noise. The
new flag lets Section 4 (and any future work) hold the variant set
constant.

## S1.2 — variant-set intersection helper

New `pipeline/misc/opensnp/intersect_pgs_variants.R`. Takes a TSV of
`panel_label, score_file_path, effect_col` rows, reads each panel's per-SNP
weights, intersects on SNP ID, and writes:

- `intersect_snplist.txt` — one SNP per line
- `intersect_summary.csv` — per-panel counts, intersection size, kept
  fraction
- `intersect_weights.rds` — per-panel weights on the intersection, aligned

Prints pairwise weight-vector correlations as a plumbing check. Section 4's
M5 (target-scored PGS correlation on a shared variant set) uses this
pattern.

# Section 2 — Real-sumstats M2

## Setup

Target: `yengo_2022_height_all.txt` (all-ancestry meta, 1.38 M variants,
median N ≈ 2.06 M).

Candidates on M2 (chr22, all 5 pops present in the block RDS from the
Round-6 `extra_pops` append):

- MELD-λ0 (analytic P-population meta target R\*)
- MELD-λ1 (P-population mega target, run once to close it out)
- EUR, EAS, AFR, CSA, AMR (single-population empirical R)

Round 6b fixes applied uniformly: eigen-clamp PSD repair on every candidate
before the masked-z solve; 2000-replicate block-bootstrap 95 % CIs;
δ = 0.01 ridge; 10 % mask fraction; 1 mask draw per block.

## 2(b) — Weights, two ways

Composition weights computed (i) from per-ancestry median N in the Yengo
per-pop files and (ii) from `bigsnpr::snp_ancestry_summary` AF-projection
on the Yengo-all EAF column.

| pop | median N   | w (paper N) | w (AF-projection) | Δ (afproj − paperN) |
| --- | ---:       | ---:        | ---:              | ---:                |
| EUR | 1,587,716  | 0.7723      | 0.7800            | +0.0077             |
| EAS |   264,013  | 0.1284      | 0.1274            | −0.0010             |
| AFR |   100,692  | 0.0490      | 0.0528            | +0.0038             |
| CSA |    44,727  | 0.0218      | 0.0193            | −0.0025             |
| AMR |    58,707  | 0.0286      | 0.0205            | −0.0081             |

<div class="note-box">

**AF-projection recovers the paper-reported composition to within 0.008 in
every super-population** on a real all-ancestry file. This is the key
Section 2 validation: most real sumstats do not report per-ancestry N, so
being able to recover the composition from allele frequencies alone is a
required capability for MELD in production, and it works. MID was
recovered at essentially zero weight and folded into EUR (nearest super-pop
in the candidate set) — the fold-in is a no-op numerically.

</div>

***

# Findings

**MELD-λ0 beats every single-population panel on M2 with real Yengo-2022
sumstats, and the ordering matches the meta composition.** EUR is closest
(+0.027 r², reflecting that EUR contributes ~78 % of the meta), AFR is
furthest (+0.306 r²). All CIs cleanly exclude zero.

**MELD-λ0 = MELD-λ1** (Δ = 0.0 ± 0.002). This is not evidence that B is
harmless in general — see the note below on why λ0 = λ1 at this
composition specifically.

**AF-projection is a viable estimator for the composition weights when
per-ancestry N is not reported.** Discrepancies vs paper-N are ≤ 0.008 in
every super-population, and produce M2 differences < 0.001 r².

## Why λ0 = λ1 here specifically (Round 7b Section B, no compute)

The between-population term B scales with products of the mixture weights:
on P populations it is
$B(i,j) = 4 \sum_p w_p (f_{p,i} - \bar f_i)(f_{p,j} - \bar f_j)$ where
$\bar f = \sum_p w_p f_p$. Because it is quadratic in $w$, B is maximised
at balanced compositions and shrinks toward zero as one population
dominates. At Yengo-2022's 78 / 13 / 5 / 2 / 3 EUR / EAS / AFR / CSA / AMR
split, the effective magnitude of B is small — the largest single Wahlund
pair (EUR × EAS with $w_{\text{EUR}} \cdot w_{\text{EAS}} \approx 0.10$)
contributes less than a fifth of what a 50/50 balanced two-population GWAS
would carry, and the other pairs are smaller still. So at this composition,
λ has almost no room to move the LD panel one way or the other, and MELD-λ0
and MELD-λ1 come out numerically tied.

Two consequences:

1. **This does not resolve the synthetic Round 6b D5 residual.** The
   synthetic Round 6 case was 50 / 50 EUR / AFR — B was proportional to
   $4 \cdot 0.5 \cdot 0.5 \cdot (f_{\text{EUR}} - f_{\text{AFR}})^2 =
   (f_{\text{EUR}} - f_{\text{AFR}})^2$, which is the largest B can be for
   a two-population meta. That is why D5 showed a real ~0.015 r² effect
   concentrated at high-|ΔAF| SNPs. The real-data Yengo case does not
   carry a similar-magnitude B. Whether the synthetic residual is stratum
   impurity or differential tagging is the Round 7b Section C question.
2. **This is a testable prediction for balanced multi-ancestry GWAS.** For
   a GWAS with a more balanced composition — GBMI, several MVP phenotypes,
   forthcoming diverse consortium efforts — B would carry appreciable
   magnitude and λ would matter considerably. The tie observed here is a
   property of the *data*, not a property of the method.

***

# Result

<div class="note-box">

**The composition effect survives on real Yengo-2022 sumstats.** MELD-λ0
beats EUR by +0.027 r² on M2 at 1KG panel scale — an order of magnitude
smaller than the synthetic MELD-λ0 vs AFR gap (0.11–0.25 r²), but
statistically clean (CI [+0.014, +0.041] excludes zero cleanly) and
ordering-consistent with the meta composition. The Round 6b synthetic
construction was construction validation; the real-data number is 0.03 vs
EUR alone. Not carrying "0.11–0.25" forward as a real-world expectation.

**AF-projection recovers composition to within 0.008 in every
super-population.** This is the specific validation that makes MELD
deployable on sumstats that do not report per-ancestry N — most sumstats.
The M2 result under AF-projection weights is 0.001 away from the result
under paper-N weights.

**MELD-λ0 = MELD-λ1 on this composition, and that is expected.** B is
weight-quadratic and negligible at 78/13/5/2/3; the tie at this composition
does not imply the tie holds at balanced compositions.

</div>

<div class="note-box">

**Superseded interpretation.** The Round 7 M2 headline attributed the +0.027
r² gain entirely to correct composition. Round 7b Section A decomposes the
gain into +0.008 r² correct-composition and +0.022 r²
shrinkage-toward-reasonable-composition (see the separate Round 7b Section
A write-up). The raw M2 tables above are still correct; the *attribution*
is refined by Section A.

</div>
